title: Japanese Cabbage Pancake with Bacon and Mayonnaise
summary: A home-style okonomiyaki-inspired cabbage pancake, crisp at the edges and tender inside, topped with savoury bacon and a creamy mayonnaise drizzle. It makes a satisfying Japanese-style dinner with simple pantry ingredients.
steps: Put the shredded cabbage and sliced spring onions in a large bowl. Toss to loosen the cabbage so it will mix evenly into the batter.
In a second bowl, whisk the plain flour, eggs, vegetable stock, soy sauce, salt and black pepper until you have a thick but pourable batter with no dry patches.
Pour the batter over the cabbage and spring onions, then fold well until all the cabbage is lightly coated.
Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add half the cabbage mixture and press it into a round pancake about 2 cm thick.
Lay half the bacon over the top of the pancake. Cook for 5–6 minutes, until the underside is deep golden and the edges look set.

Carefully flip the pancake so the bacon side is down. Cook for another 5–6 minutes, pressing gently with a spatula, until the bacon is browned and crisp and the pancake is cooked through in the centre.
Transfer to a plate and keep warm. Repeat with the remaining oil, cabbage mixture and bacon to make the second pancake.
Drizzle the pancakes with mayonnaise, scatter over sesame seeds, and serve hot, cut into wedges.
